outcome: cardiotocograph (CTG) traces (category, variability, tachycardia, bradycardia, acceleration, deceleration, uterine contractility)
cohort: 224 women with a single pregnancy of 32 weeks or more, who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.
finding: Maternal COVID-19 infection was associated with changes in CTG, primarily an increase in the baseline, although no statistically significant relationship was found between COVID-19 severity and most CTG parameters or Apgar scores.
